**Experimental mod only for testing!**

Main feature of this mod is ability to use **box32**. 
If **WoW64** mode is enabled, WoW64 Wine is used (default).
If **WoW64** mode is disabled, the regular bi-arch Wine is used with the **box32** feature. For now, some x86 OpenGL games work in **box32** mode with higher performance than in WoW64 mode.

- Built-in custom **frame generation** (_Screen effects -> Frame generation_).
- Support of **Russian** input (Unicode) from the on-screen keyboard.
- **Freedreno** OpenGL driver, **LLVMPipe** driver.
- Optional **Lorie X-server**.
- **Old VirGL** test server with better compatibility.

It is recommended to _disable WoW64_ mode with **VirGL** for better performance.

**Changes:**
- Added **vkBasalt** sharpness effects for shortcuts (from Winlator Bionic).
- Upgraded **Frame generation**: improved _motion estimation_, added _FPS multiplier_ (x2, x3, x4), added _Motion scale_, _Blending_ and _Post-processing_ adjustments, added _Engine_ options (DIS, QCOM, GLES).

releases.name: ares v148
releases.body:
ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

ares v145 has now been released.

This release contains hefty improvements to a number of ares components. Highlights include Real Time Clock support for the Game Boy Advance, improvements to the experimental PlayStation core, Sega SC-3000 support, important fixes to the Game Boy Color, as well as core improvements to the ares application itself that should improve performance and responsiveness.

Since v144, 8 contributors have created 90 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v144...v145).

**ARM7TDMI (Game Boy Advance CPU, ST018 Super Famicom coprocessor)**

- Implemented many undocumented instruction encodings
- Implemented invalid CPSR modes
- Added support for MRC, MCR, and CDP coprocessor instructions
- Allowed misalignment of the program counter in ARM mode

**Nintendo - Game Boy Color**

- Improved HDMA and GDMA timings (fixes some major graphical bugs)

**Nintendo - Game Boy Advance**

- Added support for the Real Time Clock
- Re-introduced optional Game Boy Player support

## NieR:Automata Android Recomp v0.2.7

### Español
- **Soporte multi-región y fix de modelos negros (PR #26 / PR #27):** Resolución automática `ADRP+LDR` para USA y Asia 1.0.3 (presenter y resolución dinámica mínima `0.6`) y firma ampliada de 8 instrucciones en `mesh_draw_hook` para evitar falsos matches y modelos/naves en negro.
- **Corrección de reflejos/cubemaps negros:** Añadido `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_CUBE_COMPATIBLE_BIT` en texturas `2D_ARRAY` cuadradas de `6n` capas.
- **Optimizaciones de rendimiento NVN:** Salida rápida con `memcmp` + comparación SIMD NEON ARM64 en write-backs (`apply_write_back`), pool de snapshots (`g_before_pool`) y pool de buffers spill (`g_staging_pool`) para reducir pausas de CPU y asignaciones de memoria por frame.
- **Fix Android 10 (API 29) y diagonales en mando:** Guard de `InsetsController` para evitar crashes al iniciar en Android 10 y zona muerta radial 2D para sticks físicos.

---

### English
- **Multi-region hooks & black models fix (PR #26 / PR #27):** Automatic `ADRP+LDR` slot resolution across USA and Asia 1.0.3 builds (presenter & dynamic-res floor `0.6`) plus expanded 8-instruction `mesh_draw_hook` signature to prevent black 3D models/ships.

- 整合声音、对白、亮度、纹理、植被显示与运行时内存修复，混音器默认启用。
- 修正 Mali 顶点整数属性与着色器输入类型匹配，RG477M 人物已可正常显示。

RG477M / MT6897 / Mali-G615 / Android 14 已验证安装、原版 Ver1.07 标题、声音恢复、人物显示、开场至户外与城镇流程、虚拟手柄和原游戏存档缩略图。图形组件测试 64 项中 63 通过、1 项缺私有输入跳过，运行时 8 项通过。

releases.body:
* Fixed GB, GBC and GBA games running slow on PAL (576i) 50Hz output
* Fixed JIT IRQ latency bug causing graphical artifacts
* **Restored the original controls of the games with special Wii controls** (Zelda, Mario, Metroid, Ninja Turtles, Mortal Kombat, Star Wars, Harry Potter, Medal of Honor, Boktai, The Lord of the Rings, Castlevania and the rest). # v0.0.8.2 Experimental — Stability Update & On-Screen Control Editor

Small stability update on top of `v0.0.7.9-experimental`. Still experimental — please use **EXPORT LOGS** when reporting anything.

## New: customize the on-screen controls

A **CUSTOMIZE** pill now sits next to **TOUCH** in the HUD. It opens an in-place editor:

- Tap a control to select it, then **drag** to move it.
- **S- / S+** resize, **O- / O+** change opacity.
- **BIND** cycles a button's guest input index.
- **PRESET** cycles DEFAULT → COMPACT → LEFT → RIGHT.
- **RESET** restores the original layout, **DONE** saves and exits.

Layouts are stored as normalized coordinates, so they survive rotation/window resizing and app restarts. Guest input is suppressed while the editor is open (no phantom presses), gamepad focus rules are unchanged, and **TOUCH: OFF** also leaves edit mode.

## Stability / rendering correctness (from the in-progress post-0.0.7.9 patch)

- Pixel shaders now use full FP32 with NaN-safe multiply helpers (`mulL`/`mulL1`), clamp-before-scale texture adjustment, and `isnan()` output sanitization — removes FP16 overflow/NaN artifacts without changing the guest shader set.

releases.name: v2.5.17 — Microsoft sign-in
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Microsoft sign-in no longer opens a blank white page** ([#3](https://github.com/FlameLaunchers/FlameLauncher-Android/issues/3)). Android's WebView puts `; wv` in its user agent, Microsoft reads that as an embedded browser and refuses the page — and what you get is not a message, it is an empty white screen. The marker is gone from the user agent now.

  Two more things the sign-in page needs were missing: cross-site cookies, which `login.live.com` relies on, and a `WebChromeClient`, without which the popups and dialogs the flow opens are silently dropped. The iOS build never hit any of this because WKWebView reports itself as Safari and handles those by default.
- **A sign-in page that fails to load now says why.** Main-frame errors were going nowhere, so a failure left the same white screen with nothing to report.

releases.name: v2.5.16 — Minecraft 26.4 snapshots
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 snapshots start.** A version id like `26.4-snapshot-3` splits into `26` and `4-snapshot-3`, and reading that second part as a plain integer gave nothing — so 26.4 was treated as 26.0, missed the SDL and LWJGL 3.4.3 stack, and launched on LWJGL 3.3.6 instead. The game died immediately with `NoClassDefFoundError: org/lwjgl/sdl/SDLPlatform`; the cacio lines in the crash report were a consequence, not the cause. Version numbers are now read digit by digit, so snapshot, pre-release and rc suffixes no longer hide them, and five tests cover the shapes.
- Carries the previous fix as well: on Java 24 and newer the cacio java agent is skipped, because the `sun.misc.Unsafe` calls its `premain` depends on are refused there and a failing agent takes the VM with it.

releases.name: v2.5.15 — Minecraft 26.4 starts again
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 (and anything else on Java 24 or newer) starts again.** The cacio setup loaded a java agent whose `premain` overwrites the AWT toolkit's static fields through `sun.misc.Unsafe` (`staticFieldBase`, `staticFieldOffset`, `putObject`). Those methods are refused from JDK 24 and gone in 26, and a failing agent takes the whole VM down with it — which surfaced as a cacio error at startup.

  The iOS build has always run the same cacio jars without that agent, on the same Java 25, using only `-Dawt.toolkit` and `-Xbootclasspath/a`. Android now does the same on Java 24+ and keeps the agent only for the older runtimes that still need it.

## Lemon-Project v1.6.0

A round of fixes from your logs and reports, plus three things you asked for: a Nintendo button layout for physical controllers, frontends that bring a game's update and DLC along, and the Immediate GPU fences back as an option for advanced users.

### New
- **Button layout** (Settings → Controls): **Nintendo** swaps A↔B and X↔Y of your physical controller in games, so each button presses what a Switch has in its place. For handhelds and controllers with Xbox-style labels. Menus, hotkeys and button mapping still see the buttons as labelled.

When on, the game hears that the GPU is done as soon as the work is queued, instead of waiting for it to finish. releases.name: Catherine port v0.1.6
releases.body:
## The sushi bar scene, fixed for real, and shadows for the first time (v0.1.5 was a wrong diagnosis)

v0.1.5 did not fix the *Kappa Heaven* scene of the second day. The black shots were gone, but the plates and the conveyor belt that pass right in front of the camera were missing, and a dark line floated across the picture. The explanation in the v0.1.5 notes was wrong. Please update.

What was actually wrong is a bug in how the port translates this game's shaders. Its vertex shaders come in two halves, and when the port joined them it converted depth twice. That had three effects in every version that used the original depth format (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.3 and v0.1.4):

- The near clipping plane sat at half its distance, so geometry the console cuts away was drawn. In those sushi bar shots the camera is inside a wall, and the port drew that wall over the whole shot.
- The depth buffer was squeezed into half its range (0.5 to 1), so the depth of field compared its focus settings against wrong depths. This is where the blur problems of earlier versions came from.
- The shadow maps were stored with the same wrong depth, so no cast shadow ever showed.

releases.name: v0.1.2
releases.body:
## Cutscenes and the title screen are sharp (the real fix)

Close-ups in the *Golden Playhouse* cutscenes (the ones with the black bars) could still come out blurred from edge to edge, faces included, and the title screen looked out of focus. v0.1.1 blamed a short block of shader constants; that was wrong: the depth-of-field pass never reads those bytes.

The real cause is the depth format. The game never tells the graphics API which depth range it uses, and the port assumed the OpenGL-style one, which stores depth squeezed into 0.5–1. The game's depth-of-field planes come straight from each cutscene's data and are written for a plain 0–1 depth, so a face in a close-up landed *behind* the focus plane and the whole frame got the maximum blur. When the game does not choose, the port now uses 0–1 depth, so close-ups keep the face sharp and blur only the background, as intended.

- Checked on the Flip 2: the title screen (same shot before/after: background, piano and characters go from blurred to sharp), the host's introduction, the opening credits, the opening nightmare cutscene and the first puzzle stage, at 30 fps.

# BachataS4 1.2.0

App Store: 1.2.0 (124), bundle games.bachatas4, interpreter only.

## New
- Native Metal renderer, EXPERIMENTAL and off by default. Turn it on in Settings > Runtime >
  "Native Metal renderer (Experimental)". It applies from the next game launch. MoltenVK stays

- MoltenVK queue submits are asynchronous on iOS: the emulator no longer waits on each submit.
- Metal shader compile workers run at utility QoS, so they compete less with the game threads.

- Write protection of pages a pending GPU write targets is held back; the GPU is waited for before wrapped guest pages are unmapped (God of War III boot fault).
- The copy-shader HLE drops elements past the destination buffer.
- Small read-only guest data is copied when a draw binds it.
- A buffer write skips the write-back of images it covers.
- A wait that a pending fence ends submits the queued GPU work.

releases.body:
v0.7.7 fixes the Android surface orientation: the v0.7.6 build restored the identity-preferred swapchain preTransform that had shipped in v0.7.5, and on devices reporting ROTATE_90 the composer applied that rotation a second time to an already-upright window-space blit. # Swap2-Native 0.2.0.2-beta

Less memory trouble in heavy places, a clearer "Compiling shaders" screen, and Pokémon Pokopia's shader update made short.

**Install over 0.2.0.1-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A game that slows to a crawl when the phone runs out of memory** (Zelda: Ocarina of Time entering Castle Town on a 16 GB phone fell to under 1 fps for minutes). The texture cache now notices when the phone starts swapping the game out and stops growing instead. If a game still stutters in big areas, turn on **RAM saving** (Game settings) and close other apps.
- **Zelda: Ocarina of Time on phones with 12 GB of RAM or less** uses less memory for textures and graphics memory (from Banana Native).
- **The "Compiling shaders" screen** shows its whole text on two lines (the time left and "Tap to skip" were cut off), and its bar follows the count.
- **Pokémon Pokopia** updates its shaders quickly after installing 0.2.0: about 60 shaders instead of all of them.

releases.name: Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta
releases.body:
# Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta

A fix for 0.2.0-beta: no more black screen while a game prepares its pipelines.

**Install over 0.2.0-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is translated or prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A black screen at the first start of a game** (seen with Turnip drivers, for example on a Redmagic 11 Air). Since 0.2.0, a game prepares its known pipelines before it plays (at most 90 seconds). The loading screen had already gone by then, so the game looked stuck. Now the loading screen stays and shows **Compiling shaders: N of M**; tap it to skip the rest. On Turnip the pipelines are made one at a time, so the first start takes the full 90 seconds unless you skip; the next starts are short.

Everything else is as in [0.2.0-beta](https://github.com/mamcjr/Swap2-Native/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta).

## Thanks

**moceure and the Banana Native contributors**, **enjoyerofslop / DroidPlay Core**, **Sergii "iOrange" Kudlai** (bcdec), **erickmendes22** and **EddizEge / AnkaNative**. Licenses and attribution are included in the sources.

# Swap2-Native 0.2.0-beta

Five more Switch 2 games boot, Zelda: Ocarina of Time draws its grass and gets faster, and a new graphics menu offers four upscalers with a level, plus grass and fog options.

**Install over 0.1.9.3-beta.** Games, packs, mods and saves are kept. **The shaders change:** each game updates its shader library the first time you play it after installing. Swap2-Native now speaks the Switch 2's 16 languages, works with a controller from the library to the in-game panel, has a redesigned in-game panel, and offers a frame rate cap in every game.

releases.name: v0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release of Odin.

Odin (ᚨ) is a low-level emulator of the SEGA Hikaru arcade board. It runs the programs of the real chips wherever they are known, and draws with OpenGL or Vulkan. It is a hard fork of Valkyrie, by Stefano Teso.

## Games

All six Hikaru games, two of them in two versions:

- Air Trix (`airtrix`, `airtrixo`)
- Brave Firefighters (`braveff`)
- Planet Harriers (`pharrier`)
- NASCAR Arcade (`sgnascar`, `sgnascaro`)
- Star Wars Racer Arcade (`swracer`)
- Cyber Troopers Virtual-On Force (`von4`)

They play with a keyboard, mice, gamepads, wheels with force feedback (NASCAR) or light guns (Brave Firefighters). Each game is a MAME ROM and needs the BIOS `hikaru.zip` and `mie.zip` too.

> **Release candidate.** This is the first test build of 1.3.0. It adds a lot of new features, and most of them have passed automated checks so far, with them being tested by me personally but NOT all of them. Please report anything that breaks on the issue tracker, with your platform and what you were doing.

## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and the `course-*` files together.
Tracks that use the new wind or CPU aggression settings save a newer settings block that 1.2.x cannot read. Tracks that do not use them stay readable by older builds. Keep your backup if you might go back to 1.2.x.

## New: G-Diffuser Companion (Windows and Linux)

The Windows x64, Linux x64 and Linux arm64 downloads now include the Companion, a separate desktop program in the `companion` folder inside your G-Diffuser folder. It builds the files G-Diffuser loads and checks every input before it builds. It never edits your settings, saves or stores.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.3 - Course Editor Hotfix
releases.body:
## Fixes
- Correct complete-course snapshot content binding so metadata-only edits do not reuse an incompatible retained snapshot.
- Handle terminal disk-write refusals without trapping Course Edit in its save wait loop.
- Fix the host editor's remaining 64-node admission ceiling. The supported total remains 127 nodes, including forks.
- Restore Content Library layout previews for supported tracks above 64 nodes.
- Adapt native load, overwrite, and delete confirmations to long filenames while keeping normal-size text and the Yes/No controls in place.
- Size the Course Edit information panel dynamically to fit the track title, length, and node count.

## Save compatibility — read before updating
Close the game and back up the complete installation save/state set before updating, not only the cartridge `.sav` file.

This release writes version-2 `.gcs` snapshots and still reads version 1. Older builds cannot read version-2 snapshots or packages that contain them. Before downgrading, restore the complete matching pre-upgrade save/state backup. Keeping old snapshots alone is not sufficient.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix
releases.body:
## G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix

- Fix disk-write ownership checks that could prevent Course Edit saves from completing and cause track imports to fail with MFS error 244.
- Preserve snapshot validation, rollback, and recovery protections during save and import operations.
- Add regression coverage using the production disk-write helper, including write failures and rollback.

Back up your installation's save and course-state files before updating. This hotfix does not change the course snapshot format.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.1 - The Small Improvements and Fixes Update
releases.body:
## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and `course-elements.gdxs`, `course-forks.gbs`, and
`course-settings.gks` together. Do not open snapshot-backed saves in an older executable.
The new, extended tracks that go above the original 64 node limit are not compatible with the original Expansion Kit or older tools.

## Course Edit

- Widen the native course information panel at a fixed size. Keep full 20-character names on
  one row and fit three-digit node counts without moving the buttons below it. Dynamic sizing
  is deferred.

- Raise the combined main-path and alternate-path control-point ceiling to **127**. Geometry,
  jump, effect, decoration, and junction budgets still apply; 127 points is not a guarantee
  that every layout fits.
- Add complete, content-bound save snapshots for extended courses and complete course/cup
  package sharing. Missing or mismatched required snapshot data is rejected rather than
  silently loading a truncated course.
- Keep both paths selectable after editor reload and save/reload. Show stored branch nodes

releases.body:
1.2.0 brings G-Diffuser to macOS and Android, adds an in-game updater, and is the biggest Course Edit update so far: Mouse Controls, undo, forks, lava strips from F-Zero GX, Magnet strips for the original F-Zero, and Blender-style camera controls. Thanks to everyone in the feature requests channel who shaped it.

## Before you update

- **Coming from 1.1.0, download this release by hand.** 1.1.0 has no updater. From 1.2 on, desktop builds can update themselves.
- **To install by hand,** extract the release over your existing `G-Diffuser` folder. Your `saves/`, ROM and game data stay where they are.
- **Rebuild your ROM hack archives.** Hacks now carry more of their own data, and an archive built by an older version doesn't have it.
- **Continue Cup is per hack.** An existing `gp_resume.bin` stays with the stock game, and each hack starts with no saved cup.
- **Courses that use new features need 1.2.** Forks, magnet traps, custom music and custom elements are ignored or lost on older versions.
